name: zune-png (PNG decoder)
baseline: png 0.18 (image-rs/png), the image crate's PNG decoder
verdict_reason: In its author's current run zune-png is 1.11x faster than the png crate on a baseline 8-bit image and 1.67x faster on interlaced images, but png is faster on 16-bit images (1.14x) and palette images (1.24x). The default has caught up enough that the choice depends on the image type.
tier_reason: First-party criterion results; the benchmark code is public but the machine is identified only as Darwin, with no CPU or rustc version.
claimed_speedup: Decode time, image-rs/png vs zune-png: baseline 149.3 ms vs 135.0 ms, interlaced 8bpp 232.8 ms vs 139.7 ms (zune-png 1.11x and 1.67x faster); 16 bpp 163.7 ms vs 186.3 ms, palette 28.31 ms vs 35.21 ms (png 1.14x and 1.24x faster)
workload: Decoding PNG files: 8-bit baseline, 8-bit Adam7 interlaced, 16-bit and palette images; criterion time per image.
platforms: Any; SSE and NEON intrinsics for unfiltering, scalar fallback
one_liner: Pure-Rust PNG/APNG decoder; faster than the png crate on 8-bit and interlaced images, slower on 16-bit and palette images.
how_it_is_fast: zune-png pairs its own inflate implementation (zune-inflate) with SSE and NEON intrinsics for PNG unfiltering, the two stages that dominate PNG decode time.
use_it_when: You decode many interlaced or 8-bit RGB/RGBA PNGs and PNG decoding shows up in profiles.
skip_it_when: Your images are mostly 16-bit or palette-based; the png crate was faster there.
You decode through the image crate and do not want a second PNG decoder.
caveats: Single first-party run on an unspecified Darwin machine; no x86_64 numbers are published alongside.
The png crate has itself become much faster: in the same run it decodes 2.0x to 3.3x faster than spng, while Google's 2022 benchmark had png slower than spng on large images.
The zune-image README says its decoders are "some of the fastest" without per-format qualifiers.
tradeoffs: Expands images below 8 bits per pixel to 8 bits automatically.
Smaller user base than the png crate, which the image crate uses.
